A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison. The shorter bibliography in v5 does not indicate missing scientific material.

before.justification: v4 reports original SMC experiments, including benchmark comparisons and dimensional scaling in Section 5, backward-kernel experiments in Appendix E, and additional results in Appendix F.

after.justification: v5 retains the original benchmark, dimensional-scaling, backward-kernel, and adaptation experiments in Section 5 and Appendices E–F.

M1.justification: The adaptation objectives, algorithms, and LMC/KLMC procedures are retained. Changing OABAO to OBABO in the introduction aligns it with Section 4.2 in both versions; it does not establish a different discretization.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 22 benchmark problems listed in Tables 1–3, Gaussian dimensional-scaling scenarios, and Gaussian backward-kernel comparison. Appendix coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain fixed-parameter grid search, differentiable AIS with and without variational reference tuning, SMC-MALA-ESJD, SMC-MALA-ARC, and the same backward-kernel alternatives.

E3.justification: Section 5.4 changes the stated MALA acceptance-rate target from 0.575 to 0.574. Other experimental settings are retained. This is a reported setting correction; the PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The dimensional-scaling analysis, backward-kernel comparison, adaptation-cost analysis, and adapted-schedule diagnostics test the same questions with unchanged evidence in Section 5.4 and Appendices E–F.

E5.justification: Both versions retain 32 replications and 80% empirical quantiles for the principal comparisons, and 256 replications for Figure 7. No uncertainty-reporting procedure or run count changes.

E6.justification: The plotted results and stated findings are retained, including the comparison on 20 of 22 benchmarks and the poor performance on Rats. Figure 5 remains unchanged despite the acceptance-target correction.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, guarantees, and Appendix D proofs are substantively unchanged. Kernel and transport-map symbol corrections in Sections 3.1–3.2 standardize notation without changing the mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same incremental-KL adaptation contribution, gradient-free tuning claims, convergence guarantees, and computational-cost and accuracy claims.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the qualifications about greedy optimization and adaptive-estimator bias, the dimensional-scaling interpretation, and Appendix E's restriction of the preferred backward kernel to kernels with tractable densities.

D1.justification: The documented MALA tuning hyperparameter changes from 0.575 to 0.574 in Section 5.4. Tables 4–5, Appendix B implementation details, and code-access links otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5.4 reattributes Gaussian MALA scaling and acceptance-rate guidance from Roberts and Tweedie (1996) to Roberts and Rosenthal (1998). Both works already appeared in the bibliography; broader research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: v5 makes limited wording and notation edits, corrects OABAO to OBABO, and replaces appendix-reference wording with section symbols. The narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v5 adjusts typography, line wrapping, and table-cell layout, and removes citation-page backreferences from the bibliography. Figures and table structures are retained; there is no substantive visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v5 improves internal consistency by aligning OBABO terminology with Section 4.2 and correcting kernel notation in Sections 3.1–3.2. These are modest clarity gains with unchanged results and proofs. Removing bibliography backreferences introduces a small navigation loss.
